anomaly_def.Name: Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located in the network and connection-handling layer between clients and the database server, where transport, transport-security, listener, authentication, socket I/O, or connection-slot resources cannot service the offered request rate. It is distinct from in-engine waits because the bottleneck lies in cross-host data movement and connection lifecycle rather than in statement execution. Observable phenomena: client-visible connection-establishment timeouts and connection-class error codes, increasing counters of aborted or refused connections, accumulation of half-open or wait-state sockets at the operating-system layer, established sessions accumulating client-read or client-write wait events, too-many-connections rejections with backend process or thread counts at the configured limit, oversized result sets holding backends idle while bytes are sent, and elevated network retransmission and round-trip-time metrics correlated with database latency. Possible contributing factors: network congestion, packet loss, asymmetric path size, deep firewall or application-layer proxy inspection, name-resolution or reverse-lookup delay, listener backlog and operating-system socket queue limits set too small, exhausted server-side processes or threads stalling authentication, oversized application connection pools or connection leaks, retry storms after brief outages, large result-set transfers and slow client consumers, transport-security handshake overhead, and intermediate network devices resetting idle sockets.

entry.official_definition: Write timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol write operation exceeds mysqlx_write_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network write operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
